news.title: GSC & TGV Are Hosting a Watch Party for the World Cup Final With Free-Flow Popcorn & Drinks
news.lede: There’s just something special about watching football with a crowd. Whether it’s celebrating a last-minute winner, gasping over a missed chance, or debating every refereeing decision, the experience always feels more exciting when you’re surrounded by fellow fans. With the 2026 FIFA World Cup final looming, it’s the perfect time to gather your football-loving friends and soak in the atmosphere together. Exclusively for the final match, two of Malaysia's well-known cinema chains, GSC and TGV, are set to host live watch parties.

news.title: FIFA President Gianni Infantino says he will seek re-election in March despite calls to resign
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino remains committed to standing for re-election amid renewed opposition to his candidacy after a botched plan to sell a stake in FIFA competitions to private investors, a spokesperson for the global soccer body said on Sunday.Infantino, who had previously announced that he would seek a fourth term in March next year, has faced calls to resign from UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, after his plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup and other FIFA events was scrapped amid widespread backlash in July.But the 56-year-old retains support from the African and South American confederations." The FIFA president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed.

news.title: Penalty denies New Zealand in opening game at FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: A stoppage-time penalty by Japan has denied New Zealand their first point at this year’s FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. New Zealand and Japan were tied 1-1 at the end of normal time at Stadion Miejski ŁKS Łódź when the Asian champions were awarded a penalty. The spot kick was struck home by Miyu Matsunaga, giving her a double and helping earn her the Player of the Match award. After a scoreless first half, Matsunaga was brought off the bench and she gave Japan the lead four minutes into the second spell.

news.title: Infantino reiterates intention to run for fourth term as Fifa boss
news.lede: Gianni Infantino, the head of world football's governing body Fifa, on Sunday redeclared his intention to continue until 2031 as the sport's most powerful executive despite calls for his resignation over his botched plan to sell a stake in Fifa competitions to private investors. "The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027," a Fifa spokesperson said. "Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election."
